notes: FT-DUPLICATE: non-primary version of the article coded under P00235 (arXiv 2604.03522; version of record Structural and Multidisciplinary Optimization, doi 10.1007/s00158-026-04342-6). Excluded under PROTOCOL §4 and screening_codes.md (primary version = version of record if open access, else the latest arXiv version). Evidence that 2509.05800 and 2604.03522 are versions of one article: same three authors; the arXiv HTML of both manuscripts opens with 'Journal: Structural and Multidisciplinary Optimization'; same method (ViT with a class/conditioning token, strain-energy and von Mises input fields, auxiliary volume, load and floating-material losses, FFT encoding and transfer learning for dynamic loads); same dataset construction (64×64, six load angles, one to four supports, volume fraction 30-50%); the dynamic results table is identical (Table 3 here, Table 7 in 2604.03522: 15.14/12.72/12.93/4.81% compliance error, 48.0% floating material), and the dynamic validation-sample figures carry the same caption and sample labels (Fig. 6 here, Fig. 11 there); same dynamic classical time (8900 s); the SMO version of record carries the 2604.03522 title. Adjudicator check (2026-09-24): the Springer article page for doi 10.1007/s00158-026-04342-6 lists 'Open Access: N', access type no-access, published 16 May 2026, so the primary version is the latest arXiv version, 2604.03522 v1 (pool P00235, decision-order position 416; P00034 is at position 100). The pool records are different versions, so the §11 same-version tie-break does not apply. Differences seen in 2604.03522 (not coded here): 30,000 static samples (60,000 here, Sec. 4.1), inference 1.26 s with model loading or 0.36 s preloaded (Sec. 5.5), added post-processing and generalization analyses (Sec. 5.3-5.4), and an abstract claiming fidelity beyond diffusion models. Verifier: if P00034 is kept instead of P00235, would-be coding of this version is: stratum speed; primary outcome Section 5 (33× static at 1.88% mean compliance error; alternative 4,450× dynamic at 4.81%, Table 3 decoder-layers model), chosen under §5.1 rule 4 over the earlier Table 2 quality comparison because the abstract and conclusion stress real-time, iteration-free generation against classical solvers. R1 fail (R1-unmatched): about 2 s inference vs full optimization runs while ViT-Small outputs are measurably worse (Table 2: mean compliance error 1.88%, 5.2% of samples above 30% error, volume-fraction error 1.01%, floating material 12.2%); no matching; partial if the stated 1.88% is read as the method's reported error. R2 partial (R2-inefficient-impl [inferred]; hardware unstated): implementation, solver, iteration count and hardware are not stated for either method; 66 s per 64×64 static run looks slow [inferred]; (c) n/a (64×64). R3 fail (R3-no-cost): training is 800,000 iterations at batch 256 with no time; 60,000 static and about 6,000 dynamic samples are never costed [inferred ≈1,100 h and ≈14,800 h at 66 s and 8,900 s per run]; no break-even. R4 pass (R4-verified [FE inferred]): compliance error, volume-fraction error, load discrepancy, floating-material share and the share above 30% error are reported for 500 validation samples, the same samples for all models (Section 5); the compliance evaluator is not described. Reporting (this version): n = 500 validation samples; OOD no; seeds no; failure rate yes (Table 2); timing protocol no; runtimes: dataset averages only; code and data on request (Declarations); hardware not stated. Screening code was I-SPEED.
